steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Does the name match?** in *Certificates in practice*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: `curl https://intranet.corp.example/` fails with *unable to get local issuer certificate*. Browsers on managed laptops are fine. The right fix on this Linux server?
options: Install the company's root CA into the system trust store with `update-ca-certificates`
Ask for a longer certificate validity
steps.explain: Managed laptops were given the private root. This server wasn't, so it can't complete the chain. `-k` would remove authentication entirely.
